subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WebSocket origin gate reusing checkBrowserOrigin

question: Should the Control UI origin policy intentionally become a universal pre-upgrade gate for every client that sends an `Origin` header, or must the gateway preserve its current client-aware scope?
rationale: The current contract depends on client metadata that is unavailable at `verifyClient` time, so selecting between universal enforcement and preserving existing non-UI client behavior is a security and compatibility policy decision.

options.title: Preserve client-aware scope
options.body: Keep the existing client-type boundary and use a pre-upgrade gate only when an equivalent safe classifier exists.

options.title: Adopt universal origin gating
options.body: Explicitly broaden the contract to reject every origin-bearing upgrade unless it satisfies the Control UI policy, with migration and compatibility documentation.

recommendation.title: Preserve client-aware scope
recommendation.body: Keep the existing client-type boundary and use a pre-upgrade gate only when an equivalent safe classifier exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Release history connects this contributor to the adjacent browser-origin enforcement boundary.
